conceptual assets.information: The run-time enable setting activates or disables clock-divider operation; dependent system logic relies on it to receive clock-enable events.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The setting is integrity-sensitive because its in-unit copy en is overwritten from enable_i at line 129 and cleared at line 125. It affects availability because en controls whether cnt advances at line 130, and disabling it clears the divider at line 133 so clock-enable events are withheld.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter enable_i so that en is cleared or incorrectly activated, suppressing required clock-enable events or causing unintended downstream activity.

conceptual assets.information: The generated clock-enable events pace dependent logic at the configured divider points; downstream logic relies on these output signals to advance.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The clock-enable outputs are integrity-sensitive control signals, and their values are generated from mutable divider state at lines 140-147. They affect availability because clearing cnt when en is inactive at line 133 eventually prevents the output events generated at lines 140-147.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could manipulate the enable or divider behavior to suppress, delay, or spuriously generate clk_en_o events, causing dependent logic to halt or operate incorrectly.

considered, not kept.reason: The clocks-and-resets rule excludes the external, watchdog, and debug reset requests, their synchronizer state, and reset outputs from conceptual assets; these are handled at lines 44-73.
The clocks-and-resets rule excludes clk_i and rstn_i as timing and reset inputs, declared at lines 106-107 and used at lines 122-128.

considered, not kept.concept: Divider count and internal pacing state
considered, not kept.reason: Pacing pulses excludes cnt and cnt2 as internal timing state because they only pace generation of clock-enable events, as shown by lines 131, 135, and 140-147.
The NUM_EN generic and fixed divider selections only determine build-time structure and cannot be changed or withheld at run time, as shown at lines 102-104 and 140-147.
